sections.text:
The KCEG over 
current relay can be used in all applications where over current protection is 
required, e.g. radial and ring circuits, and single and parallel feeders. 
Furthermore, the integral starting elements can be used to provide non-cascade 
operation and bus bar protection, with additional directional zone feeder 
protection available in the KCEG.

Thermal and restricted earth fault protection 
is also provided for lines and transformers. When used with the rectifier IDMT 
curve, this can provide full protection of silicon rectifiers. The low settings 
of KCEG relay are suitable for the protection of high impedance earthed 
systems. For arc suppression earthed systems

Introduction
The KCEG over 
current relay can be used in all applications where over current protection is 
required, e.g. radial and ring circuits, and single and parallel feeders. 
Furthermore, the integral starting elements can be used to provide non-cascade 
operation and bus bar protection, with additional directional zone feeder 
protection available in the KCEG.
Thermal and restricted earth fault protection 
is also provided for lines and transformers. When used with the rectifier IDMT 
curve, this can provide full protection of silicon rectifiers. The low settings 
of KCEG relay are suitable for the protection of high impedance earthed 
systems. For arc suppression earthed systems

Test Steps
Connect the current and voltage leads of a tester unit 
 to the relay points according to the drawings and scheme.
Inject current and voltage to each couple of points 
 till the red flag of the device displays.
Repeat the steps for each pair of points according to 
 the test sheet.
Record the results.

Testing the Relay and Protection Outputs
Carefully follow these test procedure steps
Verify the test result match the relay setting. If not consult 
 technical services.
Test trip the circuit breaker associated with the relay.
Trip Test
Request the operator to switch on the main circuit breaker.
Operate the output auxiliary contact by injection to trip the 
 circuit breaker.
Check that the circuit breaker tripped.
